unit.title: What agents are, and when to trust them

lesson.title: From chatbot to agent
lesson.subtitle: What turns a chatbot that talks into an agent that acts

video.title: From chatbot to agent
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)

chapters.label: Agents around you, and the lab

scenes.visual: A list: Confident, but made up; How could it check?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked a chatbot for 6B’s timetable for tomorrow. It wrote a lovely, confident timetable, all made up! It never looked at our real one. So what would make it actually check?

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: from a chatbot that talks to an agent that acts.

scenes.visual: A list: Writes text back to you; Predicts likely words; Can’t look up or act alone.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A chatbot is a language model that writes text back to you. It predicts likely words, one small piece at a time. On its own, it can’t look anything up or do anything.

scenes.visual: A list: Timetable; Weather; Calculator; Reminder.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An agent is a language model in a loop with tools. Tools are small programs it can ask for: a timetable, the weather, a calculator, a reminder. The model writes a request for a tool, and the app runs it.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So, an AI agent is a language model that uses tools to get a job done. It reads your request, plans, calls a tool and reads the result. Then it answers, or calls another tool first.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: weather{"place":"Kafi", …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s a real one, from Darsi Tiny, a small model that runs on your phone. I asked: what’s the weather in Kafi tomorrow? It planned to check the weather, then wrote this call: the tool’s name, the place and the day.

scenes.visual: A list: The app runs the tool; Result: sunny, 35°C, 10% rain; The model writes the answer; That’s the loop.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The app runs the tool and adds the result: sunny, a high of thirty-five, a ten percent chance of rain. Darsi Tiny reads that and answers. Request, plan, call, result, answer: that’s the loop.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! In an agent, who actually runs the weather tool?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The app. The model only writes text: a plan, a call, an answer. The app runs the tool and hands back the result. That matters: the app is where we can check things before they happen.

scenes.visual: A list: A phone assistant sets an alarm; An AI assistant: a maps tool, then traffic; At school: timetable, reminders, books.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: You may already meet agents. A phone assistant that sets an alarm. An AI assistant that finds a route with a maps tool, then checks the traffic. At school, an agent could read the timetable, set reminders or find library books.

scenes.visual: A list: Pick a request, press One step; Kafi to Dala: two tools; What it sees: one text.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: inside an agent’s loop
scenes.narration: In the app, pick a request and press One step: the plan, the call, the result and the answer appear in turn. Try the trip from Kafi to Dala, with two tools. And open What Darsi Tiny sees: it’s all one text.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. My chatbot made up a timetable. What would turn it into an agent that checks?

scenes.visual: Summary points: A chatbot talks; an agent acts; Request, plan, call, result, answer; The model writes; the app runs.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A chatbot talks; an agent acts · Request, plan, call, result, answer · The model writes; the app runs
scenes.narration: A timetable tool it can call. Remember: a chatbot talks, while an agent uses tools to act. The loop is request, plan, call, result, answer. The model writes, and the app runs the tools.

scenes.visual: A list: Play “Human agent”; The model writes a plan and a call; The tool answers from the board; Did the answer come from the result?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play Human agent. One pupil is the model and writes a plan and a tool call. Another is the timetable tool and answers from the board. The class checks: did the answer come from the result?

checkpoints.prompt: In an agent, who actually runs the weather tool?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the model only writes a call as text. The app runs the tool and adds the result, so the app is where things can be checked.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the model only writes text. The app reads the call, runs the tool and hands back the result.

checkpoints.prompt: A chatbot made up a timetable. What would turn it into an agent that checks?

options.text: A timetable tool it can call, run by the app

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — with a timetable tool, the model can ask for the real timetable and answer from the result instead of inventing one.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — sounding sure or writing more doesn’t make it right. A tool lets it look at the real timetable.
